name: TCS
tagline: TCS hires freshers through the National Qualifier Test (NQT) into Ninja, Digital and Prime tracks.
process: A single online NQT (Foundation + optional Advanced sections) decides your track, then a combined Technical → Managerial → HR interview.

rounds.expect: This is the gating section: numerical ability, verbal ability, and reasoning ability, with no negative marking in 2026. You must clear the Foundation cutoff for your Advanced section to even be evaluated. Sections are individually timed, so you cannot bank leftover minutes.
themes: Time-speed-distance and time-and-work word problems under a tight per-question clock
Data interpretation from a small table or chart
Reading comprehension plus sentence-correction and para-jumble items
Percentages, ratios, and profit-loss quick calculations
prepare: Drill sectional timing on free question sets from GeeksforGeeks TCS NQT guide and PrepInsta free tier
Memorize squares, cubes, and common fraction-to-percent conversions to save seconds
Practice full-length timed mocks so section switching feels natural
Revise grammar rules (subject-verb agreement, tenses) for the verbal block
mistakes: Spending too long on one hard question and running out of time on easy points
Ignoring the verbal section because it feels 'soft' when it carries real cutoff weight
Not practicing on-screen calculator and no-rough-paper conditions
signals: Consistent accuracy across all three sub-sections, not just one strong area
Speed that shows comfort with mental math

rounds.expect: Only students aiming for Digital or Prime roles typically need strong Advanced performance. It combines advanced quant/reasoning MCQs (about 14-16 in 25 min) with two coding problems in roughly 90 minutes. Coding is evaluated on passing test cases, so partial solutions still earn partial credit.
themes: Implement a solution to a string or array manipulation problem from a plain-English spec
Write a small program using loops and conditionals that handles edge cases like empty input
Basic pattern-printing or number-theory problem (primes, GCD, factorial)
A problem needing a simple data structure such as a stack or hash map
Harder aptitude: permutations-combinations, probability, advanced series
prepare: Solve 30-40 easy problems in C, Java, or Python on HackerRank and pay attention to input parsing
Practice reading input from stdin and printing formatted output exactly as required
Handle edge cases explicitly (zero, negatives, single element) since hidden test cases target them
Time yourself at 40-45 min per problem to build a coding rhythm
mistakes: Writing logic that works on the sample but fails hidden edge cases
Getting stuck on input/output formatting rather than the algorithm
Leaving both problems half-done instead of fully finishing one
signals: Working code that passes most hidden test cases
Ability to translate a word problem into correct logic quickly

rounds.expect: Usually part of one combined panel. The interviewer probes the languages and projects on your resume, core CS subjects, and simple problem-solving. Depth scales with the role you are targeting; Prime candidates get harder questions than Ninja.
themes: Walk through your main project: what problem it solved and your specific contribution
Difference between two related OOP concepts you claim to know
A basic DBMS query or normalization idea
Explain a data structure you used and why
A short logic question you reason aloud
prepare: Prepare a 60-second and a 3-minute version of each resume project
Revise OOP, DBMS (joins, normalization), OS basics, and one language deeply
Rehearse explaining code you actually wrote, not just theory
Do a mock interview with a peer focused on 'why' follow-ups
mistakes: Listing skills on the resume you cannot defend under questioning
Memorizing definitions but failing when asked to apply them
Freezing on a simple question instead of thinking aloud
signals: Honest, specific ownership of your project work
Solid grasp of fundamentals over buzzwords
Willingness to reason through something you don't immediately know

rounds.expect: Often merged with the technical panel. Considered the more relaxed part; the interviewer gauges maturity, how you handle pressure, teamwork, and whether you will actually join and stay. Scenario and situational questions are common.
themes: How you handled a conflict or a missed deadline in a team project
Why TCS specifically and what you know about the company
A hypothetical: a teammate isn't contributing, what do you do
How you keep learning new technologies
Willingness to relocate and work in any domain
prepare: Prepare 2-3 STAR-format stories about teamwork and problem-solving
Read TCS's current service lines and recent news so 'why TCS' is genuine
Practice staying calm and structured under a stress or curveball question
Decide honestly on relocation and shift flexibility so answers are consistent
mistakes: Giving generic 'I want to grow' answers with no specifics
Sounding unsure about joining or relocating (reads as high attrition risk)
Being unable to describe any real teamwork experience
signals: Genuine interest in TCS and the role

rounds.expect: The final and usually quickest step. Covers documentation, willingness to sign the service agreement, relocation, shift timings, salary structure, and joining timelines. Rarely eliminatory unless there are red flags in communication or a mismatch on basic terms.
themes: Tell me about yourself and your strengths
Are you comfortable with the service bond and relocation
Your expectations from your first job
Any gaps in education and how you spent them
prepare: Have documents and academic records organized and ready
Know the compensation and bond terms so you can respond confidently
Prepare a crisp 'tell me about yourself' pitch
Have honest explanations ready for any academic gaps or backlogs
mistakes: Negotiating aggressively on a fixed fresher package
Hesitating on the service agreement, which is standard
Poor spoken clarity after clearing everything else
signals: Overall fit and readiness to join

topics: Basic DSA: arrays, strings, stacks, hash maps
Clear articulation of your resume projects
eligibility: B.E/B.Tech/M.E/M.Tech/MCA/M.Sc across all branches; minimum 60% aggregate (some drives phrase it as 6.0 CGPA) in 10th, 12th, and graduation; no active backlogs at the time of the drive; gap norms vary by drive but typically a maximum 2-year education gap. Exact cutoffs vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Refresh quantitative aptitude fundamentals and take a diagnostic mock to find weak areas
Days 4-6: Verbal ability and reasoning daily sets plus grammar rules
Days 7-9: Code 30-40 easy problems focusing on I/O parsing and edge cases
Days 10-11: Two full-length timed NQT-style mocks; review every wrong answer
Days 12-13: Prepare resume project explanations and OOP/DBMS/OS revision
Day 14: Mock technical and HR interview; organize documents
prepC: Day 1: Two timed aptitude+reasoning mocks and revise grammar; skim your two strongest DSA topics
Day 2 morning: Solve 6-8 easy coding problems end to end with correct I/O
Day 2 afternoon: Rehearse resume projects, 'why TCS', and standard HR answers out loud

faq.q: What is the difference between Ninja, Digital, and Prime?
faq.a: They are salary/role tiers decided largely by your NQT and interview performance. Ninja is the base fresher package, Digital is higher and expects stronger technical depth, and Prime is the top tier with the hardest interview bar and best pay.

faq.q: Do I need to clear the Advanced coding section for a base offer?
faq.a: For the base Ninja role, strong Foundation performance is the main gate. The Advanced section (including coding) matters most when you are targeting Digital or Prime roles.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in the NQT?
faq.a: As reported for 2026 there is no negative marking, so attempt every question. Manage time per section since sections are individually timed.

faq.q: Are separate technical, managerial, and HR rounds guaranteed?
faq.a: In recent drives they are frequently combined into one panel interview of 30-60 minutes. Prepare for all three types of questions in a single sitting.

faq.q: Does a backlog disqualify me?
faq.a: An active (uncleared) backlog at the time of the drive typically disqualifies you. Cleared backlogs are usually acceptable, but confirm per-drive rules.

faq.q: Can one NQT score be used for multiple companies?
faq.a: Yes, the NQT is a common qualifier whose score can be shared with multiple participating employers, which is a key advantage of writing it.

overview: TCS runs India's largest fresher intake through its National Qualifier Test (NQT), a standardized online exam whose score routes you into one of three roles: Ninja, Digital, or Prime. What makes TCS distinctive is that a single NQT score can qualify you for multiple companies, and the interview is usually one long combined panel rather than separate days.

comp.note: India's largest services firm; mass-hiring bands are modest (Ninja/Digital) and real gains come from clearing the Prime test, internal promotions, or a lateral rejoin.

levels.note: Digital band pays ₹7 LPA and Prime ₹9–11.5 LPA if you clear the advanced coding test
Most freshers plateau here until first promotion; variable ~10%
Hot skills (cloud/SAP/data) and manager track push the top end

breakdown: Base is ~85–90% of CTC; variable/QPLC is small (~7–12%) and rarely paid in full
No meaningful joining bonus for freshers; laterals may get a small retention/joining component
Fresher bands: Ninja ₹3.5–4 LPA, Digital ~₹7 LPA, Prime ₹9–11.5 LPA — decided by the aptitude/coding test
Biggest jumps come from internal band promotion (Y→C1→C3A→C3B→C4) or leaving and rejoining as a lateral

name: Infosys
sector: IT services · SE / SP / DSE tracks
tagline: Infosys hires via an online assessment then technical + HR interviews; SP/DSE run a pure coding test.
process: System Engineer uses aptitude + pseudocode + verbal; Specialist Programmer / Digital Specialist Engineer use a 3-problem coding test. Then a technical interview and HR.

rounds.expect: Around 65 questions across quantitative, logical reasoning, and verbal ability with no negative marking. Sections are timed and act as the primary filter. For programmer tracks, a pseudocode or coding component is added on top.
themes: Data interpretation and arithmetic word problems
Verbal: reading comprehension and error spotting
prepare: Practice free sectional sets and take timed mocks
For programmer roles, drill pseudocode reading on GeeksforGeeks
Build mental-math speed for the quant section
Revise grammar and practice RC skimming techniques
mistakes: Under-preparing verbal, which many technical students neglect
Skipping pseudocode practice for programmer tracks

rounds.expect: The System Engineer track usually has one to two interview rounds; the higher DSE/programmer tracks have more, with a stronger coding component. Expect resume-driven questions, core CS subjects, and simple problem-solving; harder DSA appears for programmer roles.
themes: Explain a project and the tech choices you made
OOP principles with real examples from your code
Write or dry-run a small algorithm (string/array)
OS or networking basics depending on your resume
prepare: Deeply revise one language plus OOP, DBMS, and OS
Solve easy-medium DSA if targeting programmer tracks
Prepare clear, honest project walkthroughs
Do a mock technical interview with follow-up questions
mistakes: Weak project ownership when questioned deeply
For programmer roles, being unable to write clean code live
signals: Clear coding logic (especially for programmer roles)

rounds.expect: Assesses communication, cultural fit, flexibility on location and shift, and joining logistics. Generally not heavily eliminatory unless communication is poor or answers are inconsistent.
themes: Tell me about yourself and your strengths/weaknesses
Why Infosys and why this role
Willingness to relocate and work across domains
How you handle pressure or feedback
prepare: Prepare a concise personal pitch
Research Infosys's business and recent initiatives
Have honest, consistent answers on relocation and flexibility
Keep documents ready
mistakes: Generic answers with no company knowledge
Inconsistency between technical and HR answers

eligibility: Minimum 60% or 6.0 CGPA in Class 10, Class 12, and graduation; strictly no active backlogs at application. Higher tracks like Power Programmer typically expect 7.5+ CGPA plus strong HackWithInfy/InfyTQ performance. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Diagnostic aptitude mock; rebuild weak quant topics
Days 4-6: Reasoning and verbal daily sets
Days 7-9: Pseudocode practice and easy DSA if targeting programmer roles
Days 10-11: Full timed mocks, review mistakes
Days 12-13: Core CS revision and project prep
Day 14: Mock technical and HR rounds
prepC: Day 1: Two aptitude mocks plus pseudocode drills; revise OOP and DBMS
Day 2 morning: Solve easy DSA problems and prepare project explanations
Day 2 afternoon: Rehearse HR answers and research Infosys

faq.q: Is InfyTQ certification mandatory?
faq.a: It is not strictly mandatory, but certified candidates are often preferred, shortlisted faster (especially off-campus), and better positioned for the programmer tracks.

faq.q: What is the difference between System Engineer and Specialist/Power Programmer?
faq.a: System Engineer is the standard fresher role. Specialist and Power Programmer are higher-paid tracks with a much harder coding bar, often gated by HackWithInfy or InfyTQ performance and higher CGPA.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in the online test?
faq.a: As reported, Infosys does not use negative marking, so attempt everything within the section time limits.

faq.q: How many interview rounds are there?
faq.a: The System Engineer track usually has one to two rounds combining technical and HR. Programmer tracks tend to have more rounds with deeper coding.

faq.q: Do backlogs matter?
faq.a: Yes, you generally need no active backlogs at the time of applying. Confirm the exact rule for your specific drive.

faq.q: How coding-heavy is the standard track?
faq.a: For System Engineer, expect basic-to-easy problem solving and pseudocode. Serious DSA is mainly for the programmer tracks.

overview: Infosys hires freshers through a no-negative-marking online aptitude test followed by technical and HR interviews, with parallel higher tracks (Specialist Programmer and Power Programmer) that demand serious coding. What sets Infosys apart is the weight it gives to InfyTQ and HackWithInfy performance, which can fast-track you into the better-paid programmer roles.

comp.note: Similar mass-hiring economics to TCS; System Engineer is the base band, Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE/Power Programmer) pays far more, and JL promotions drive raises.

levels.note: Digital Specialist Engineer / Power Programmer band pays ₹6.5–9 LPA
Laterals command a clear premium over internal promotees
Manager or specialist-architect track reaches the top band

breakdown: Base ~85–90% of CTC; variable ~8–12%, tied to company + unit performance
Fresher CTC set by hiring track: SE ₹3.6–4.5 LPA vs DSE/Power Programmer ₹6.5–9 LPA
Minimal joining bonus for freshers; laterals negotiate joining/retention pay
Raises come mainly through JL band promotions and switching to in-demand skills (cloud, AI/data, SAP)

name: Wipro
tagline: Wipro hires freshers through the Elite National Level Talent Hunt: aptitude + essay + coding, then interviews.
process: An SHL-administered online test (aptitude + written essay + 2 coding problems), then a technical interview and HR.

rounds.expect: A compact aptitude block (quant, logical reasoning, verbal) plus a written essay on a given topic, with no negative marking. The essay is genuinely evaluated for structure, grammar, and coherence, so it is not a throwaway.
themes: Essay on a general or opinion topic in a fixed word range
prepare: Practice a 200-300 word structured essay in 15-20 minutes
Drill timed aptitude sections on free platforms
Revise grammar so the essay reads cleanly
Take full NLTH-style mocks including the essay
mistakes: Treating the essay casually or leaving it incomplete
Grammatical errors and no clear intro-body-conclusion in the essay
Poor time management between MCQs and essay

rounds.expect: Engineering graduates across branches face 2-3 coding problems. Data structures and simple dynamic programming are the most-tested areas. Strong performance can push you toward the Turbo/Elite premium track.
themes: Array or string manipulation with edge cases
A problem using a stack, queue, or hash map
Simple recursion or a basic DP problem
prepare: Solve 30-40 easy-medium problems on HackerRank/LeetCode
Practice input parsing and exact output formatting
Drill basic DSA: arrays, strings, stacks, hashing, simple DP
Time yourself to finish at least one problem fully
mistakes: Passing samples but failing hidden edge cases
Not attempting the harder problem at all

rounds.expect: Covers coding, DBMS, OS, and OOP fundamentals along with your resume projects. Depth varies by track; premium-track candidates get harder questions.
themes: Explain and defend a project decision
SQL query writing and DBMS basics
OS concepts (process, thread, deadlock at a basic level)
Dry-run or explain a coding solution
prepare: Revise DBMS, OS, OOP, and one language thoroughly
Prepare concise project walkthroughs
Practice explaining code aloud
Do a mock technical interview
mistakes: Being unable to write basic SQL

rounds.expect: Assesses motivation, relocation willingness, team fit, and salary/joining expectations, plus acceptance of the standard service agreement.
themes: Why Wipro and why IT services
prepare: Prepare a crisp self-introduction
Research Wipro's services and values
Have consistent answers on relocation and the bond
Keep documents organized
mistakes: Hesitating on the standard service agreement

eligibility: B.E/B.Tech/M.E/M.Tech (typically any branch); minimum 60% independently in 10th, 12th, and degree; no active backlogs, though cleared backlogs are usually acceptable. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic and weak-topic rebuild; start essay practice
Days 4-6: Reasoning, verbal, and daily timed essays
Days 7-9: Code 30+ easy-medium DSA problems
Days 10-11: Full NLTH mocks including essay and coding
Days 12-13: Core CS revision and project prep
Day 14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock plus two timed essays; revise DBMS/OOP
Day 2 morning: Solve 6-8 DSA problems with correct I/O
Day 2 afternoon: Prepare projects and rehearse HR answers

faq.q: Does the essay actually matter?
faq.a: Yes. The NLTH essay is scored for structure, grammar, and coherence, so treat it as a real evaluated component, not filler.

faq.q: What are the salary tracks?
faq.a: Wipro hires through a standard track and higher Elite/Turbo tracks. Strong coding performance can route you into the premium track with better pay.

faq.q: Is there negative marking?
faq.a: The NLTH aptitude test is reported to have no negative marking, so attempt every question.

faq.q: Are cleared backlogs a problem?
faq.a: Active backlogs typically disqualify you, but cleared backlogs are usually acceptable. Confirm per drive.

faq.q: How hard is the coding round?
faq.a: Expect 2-3 problems at easy-to-medium level, with data structures and simple DP most common. Finishing at least one problem cleanly is important.

faq.q: Is there a service agreement?
faq.a: Wipro fresher offers commonly include a standard service agreement. Be ready to discuss and accept it in the HR round.

overview: Wipro hires freshers through its National Level Talent Hunt (NLTH), a short aptitude test paired with a mandatory essay and a coding section for engineering graduates, followed by technical and HR interviews. The written essay is a distinctive step: your written English is actually scored, not just your MCQs, and top coders can be routed to premium Turbo/Elite tracks.

comp.note: Value bands are lean; Project Engineer is the mass fresher role while WILP/Turbo and hot-skill laterals earn more, with promotions (A→B→C bands) driving growth.

levels.note: Turbo/premium hiring and WILP grads land ₹6–8 LPA
Variable ~10%; first promotion is the key jump
Laterals paid well above internal peers
Cloud/data/cyber skills push the higher end
Manager or Wipro consulting track reaches the top

breakdown: Base ~85–90% of CTC; variable ~8–12%
Fresher pay depends on track: standard ₹3.5–4 LPA vs Turbo/premium ₹6–8 LPA
Little to no fresher joining bonus; laterals negotiate joining components
Band promotions and hot-skill moves (cloud, cyber, data) drive the biggest raises

name: Accenture
sector: IT services · Associate SE / Full Stack
tagline: Accenture runs a 4-stage funnel: cognitive+technical assessment, coding, communication, then interview.
process: A cognitive & technical assessment (elimination), a coding round, a spoken-English assessment, then a combined technical + HR interview.

rounds.expect: An elimination stage combining cognitive ability (verbal, critical reasoning, numerical) with technical MCQs on fundamentals like networking, cloud basics, and common sense of pseudocode. You must clear cutoffs in each subsection.
prepare: Practice cognitive-style questions on free platforms
Revise fundamentals MCQs across CS subjects
Do timed mocks that mix aptitude and tech MCQs
Practice pseudocode tracing
mistakes: Rushing attention-to-detail items and losing easy marks

rounds.expect: An elimination round with a small number of coding problems (often two) in a language of your choice. Higher scores can qualify you for the Advanced ASE track, which pays more and has a deeper technical interview.
themes: Logic problem using loops and conditionals
A problem needing a hash map or simple sorting
prepare: Solve 25-40 easy problems on HackerRank/LeetCode
Practice exact I/O formatting
Handle edge cases explicitly
Aim to fully finish problems, not partially
mistakes: Ignoring this round when targeting only the base ASE role
signals: Higher scores for the Advanced ASE track

rounds.expect: A separate scored module (often automated) testing pronunciation, fluency, listening, and grammar. It is a real gate: weak spoken English can end your candidacy even with strong coding.
themes: Read-aloud passages for pronunciation and fluency
Describe an image or situation aloud
prepare: Practice reading English passages aloud clearly and steadily
Record yourself and check pace and clarity
Revise common grammar rules
Do free spoken-English drills daily for a week
mistakes: Speaking too fast or mumbling on read-aloud tasks
Long pauses that hurt fluency scores
Grammatical slips in the writing items

rounds.expect: Often a combined final round. Technical questions cover your resume, one language, and CS basics; HR portion covers motivation, relocation, and joining. Advanced ASE candidates face a deeper technical dive.
themes: Project walkthrough and your specific role
OOP and one language in depth
prepare: Revise one language, OOP, DBMS, and OS
Prepare crisp project explanations
Research Accenture's business and values
Practice HR answers on motivation and flexibility

eligibility: Typically 60% aggregate or equivalent CGPA throughout Class 10, Class 12, and all graduation semesters, with no active backlogs at application. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Cognitive aptitude diagnostic and rebuild weak areas
Days 4-5: Daily spoken-English read-aloud and grammar practice
Days 6-8: Technical MCQ revision plus pseudocode tracing
Days 9-11: Code 30+ easy problems with clean I/O
Days 12-13: Full mock (cognitive + coding + communication)
Day 14: Mock technical/HR interview and project prep
prepC: Day 1: Cognitive mock, pseudocode drills, and 30 min read-aloud practice
Day 2 morning: Solve easy coding problems and revise CS MCQs
Day 2 afternoon: Rehearse spoken answers and prepare projects

faq.q: Why is the Communication Assessment a separate gate?
faq.a: Accenture is client-facing at scale, so spoken and written English is formally scored as its own elimination step. Weak communication can fail you regardless of coding strength.

faq.q: Can a strong section offset a weak one?
faq.a: No. Each assessment has its own cutoff. You must clear every gate independently to move forward.

faq.q: What is the difference between ASE and Advanced ASE?
faq.a: ASE is the base engineer role. Advanced ASE (higher grade) pays more and requires a higher coding score plus a deeper technical interview.

faq.q: How coding-heavy is it?
faq.a: The base coding round is easy-level with a few problems. Serious depth matters mainly if you are targeting the Advanced ASE track.

faq.q: Do backlogs disqualify me?
faq.a: You generally need no active backlogs at application. Confirm the exact rule for your drive.

faq.q: How long does the whole process take?
faq.a: Campus drives are faster (about 2-4 weeks); off-campus can take 6-12 weeks from test to offer.

overview: Accenture's fresher process is a series of independent elimination gates: a communication assessment, a cognitive ability test, a technical MCQ assessment, and a coding round, before a combined technical/HR interview. What makes it distinctive is that each gate has its own cutoff, so you cannot compensate a weak section with a strong one, and a spoken-English (Communication Assessment) module is a formal scored step.

comp.note: Pays above Indian-heritage peers; ASE is the fresher band, promotions run through levels (13→12→11→9…) and Advanced Technology Centers plus specialized skills lift comp.

levels.note: Base higher than TCS/Infosys freshers; small variable
Annual promotion cycle plus market-adjustment raises
Bonus + equity/awards grow at higher levels
Consulting and specialist-architect tracks reach the top

breakdown: Base ~80–88% of CTC; variable/bonus ~10–15% and better-paid than heritage peers
No large fresher joining bonus, but mid/senior laterals often get sign-on and equity awards
US hiring exists but is small relative to India; India comp is the reference here
Growth via yearly promotion cycle, market adjustments, and moving into hot skills or people-management

name: Cognizant
tagline: Cognizant hires through GenC, GenC Pro and GenC Next tracks via an AMCAT-based assessment then interviews.
process: Aptitude + verbal + reasoning (plus coding for Pro/Next) and an eliminating communication round, then a technical interview (deeper for GenC Next) and HR.

rounds.expect: Combines a communication/English section with quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, and verbal ability. Acts as the first elimination filter with sectional expectations.
prepare: Take timed aptitude mocks on free platforms
Revise grammar and vocabulary
Practice DI and reasoning daily
Do full communication-plus-aptitude mocks

rounds.expect: Technical MCQs and, for engineering/advanced clusters, coding. Depending on the skill cluster you may see Java, SQL, Python, C#, web basics, or cloud fundamentals. GenC Next expects genuine coding and full-stack awareness.
themes: Web fundamentals (HTML/CSS/JS basics for relevant clusters)
A coding problem on arrays/strings (advanced track)
prepare: Revise the language/cluster relevant to the role
Practice SQL queries and DBMS basics
For GenC Next, solve easy-medium DSA problems
Do technical MCQ mocks
mistakes: Preparing the wrong cluster's tech stack
Under-preparing coding for the advanced track
signals: Solid fundamentals in the relevant stack

rounds.expect: A resume-driven technical discussion covering your language, projects, and CS basics, with more coding depth for GenC Next candidates.
themes: A small logic or coding problem
prepare: Prepare crisp project explanations
Revise OOP, DBMS, and one language
Practice explaining code aloud
Do a mock technical interview with follow-ups
mistakes: Freezing on a simple logic question

rounds.expect: Evaluates soft skills, communication, cultural alignment, motivations, and joining logistics including relocation and the service agreement.
themes: Tell me about yourself and your background
Comfort with the internship/bond terms (advanced track)
prepare: Prepare a concise self-introduction
Research Cognizant's business and culture
Have consistent flexibility answers
Keep documents ready

topics: One language relevant to your cluster (Java/Python/C#)
eligibility: More than 60% in 10th and 12th and minimum 60% in graduation; qualifications typically BE/B.Tech/ME/M.Tech/MCA; maximum gap of about 1 year after Class 12 or between semesters; no active backlogs. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic and weak-topic rebuild
Days 4-5: Communication/English and verbal practice
Days 6-8: Technical MCQs and SQL for your cluster
Days 9-11: Coding practice (heavier for GenC Next)
Days 12-13: Full mock assessment and project prep
Day 14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock, English practice, and SQL revision
Day 2 morning: Cluster tech revision plus easy coding problems
Day 2 afternoon: Project prep and HR answer rehearsal

faq.q: What is the difference between GenC and GenC Next?
faq.a: GenC is for candidates with basic programming ability; GenC Next is for strong coders with full-stack skills, includes a paid internship, and offers a higher, differential package.

faq.q: Which tech stack should I prepare?
faq.a: It depends on your assigned skill cluster. Confirm whether it is Java, Python, C#, web, or cloud focused and prepare accordingly.

faq.q: How important is communication?
faq.a: Very. There is a dedicated communication assessment and the HR round weighs soft skills, since roles are often client-facing.

faq.q: Is coding mandatory for GenC?
faq.a: Programming knowledge is recommended and increasingly expected, though the base GenC track is lighter on coding than GenC Next.

faq.q: Do backlogs and gaps matter?
faq.a: You typically need no active backlogs and a limited education gap (often up to about a year). Confirm the exact rule per drive.

faq.q: Is there an internship before joining?
faq.a: The advanced GenC Next track commonly includes a mandatory paid internship period before the differential salary applies.

overview: Cognizant hires freshers through its GenC family of programs, with a communication assessment, an aptitude-plus-technical assessment, and technical and HR interviews. What is distinctive is the split between GenC (for candidates with basic programming) and GenC Next/GenC Pro (for strong coders with full-stack ability), where the advanced track includes a paid internship and a differential, higher package.

comp.note: Programmer Analyst Trainee is the fresher base; GenC/GenC Next/Elevate premium tracks pay much more, and promotions plus laterals in digital skills drive comp.

levels.note: GenC Next/Elevate premium tracks pay ₹6.5–9 LPA
Manager track and hot skills lift the top
Specialist-architect or delivery-leadership reaches the peak

breakdown: Base ~85–90% of CTC; variable ~10–12% tied to performance
Fresher pay by track: standard GenC ₹4–5 LPA vs GenC Next/Elevate ₹6.5–9 LPA
Minimal fresher joining bonus; laterals negotiate joining/retention pay
Raises come via promotions and shifting into digital/cloud/AI skill lines

name: Capgemini
tagline: Capgemini uses the Exceller assessment (pseudocode, English, game-based aptitude) then interviews.
process: Pseudocode MCQs, English, and a game-based cognitive test; a coding round for the Senior Analyst track; then technical + HR.

rounds.expect: Around 25 questions testing your ability to trace pseudocode logic, predict output, and understand loops, conditionals, and basic data structures without any specific language syntax.
themes: Trace the output of a loop-based pseudocode block
Predict the result of nested conditionals
Identify what a small algorithm computes
prepare: Practice pseudocode tracing on GeeksforGeeks and free banks
Strengthen core programming logic (loops, conditions, arrays)
Do timed pseudocode sets
Review basic data structures conceptually
mistakes: Confusing language-specific habits with pseudocode conventions

rounds.expect: About 30 questions on vocabulary, grammar, and reasoning: synonyms/antonyms, subject-verb agreement, modifiers, voice conversion, and critical reasoning. It is a real gate.
prepare: Revise core grammar rules systematically
Build vocabulary with daily word lists

rounds.expect: Around 60 questions in 60 minutes covering quantitative aptitude, verbal ability, and logical reasoning, with no negative marking. It is the first elimination filter.
prepare: Take timed 60-in-60 mocks
Build quant speed
Practice reasoning daily
Revise grammar and RC
mistakes: Poor pacing at one minute per question

rounds.expect: MCQs on core CS subjects: data structures, OOP, DBMS, OS, and one or more programming languages. Tests breadth of fundamentals before the coding round.
prepare: Revise DS, OOP, DBMS, and OS
Practice technical MCQ sets
Review one language's syntax and concepts
Practice output prediction

rounds.expect: One or more coding problems at roughly LeetCode Easy-to-Medium level, testing data structures and problem-solving with correct handling of test cases.
themes: Problem using a hash map or stack
prepare: Solve 30-40 easy-medium problems
Practice exact I/O and edge cases
Drill core DSA
Time yourself to finish problems

rounds.expect: Covers motivation, communication, relocation, and joining. Usually the final, lighter step. For JMT roles the emphasis shifts toward communication and business aptitude.
prepare: Prepare a concise self-introduction
Research Hexaware's business
Have consistent flexibility answers
Keep documents ready

eligibility: B.E/B.Tech with 60% aggregate or 6.0 CGPA and no active backlogs for the GET track; postgraduates (any discipline) for the JMT track (largely PMO/business-ops). Drives run across cities like Chennai, Mumbai, and Pune. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic and weak-topic rebuild
Days 4-5: Technical MCQ revision (DS, OOP, DBMS, OS)
Days 6-8: Code 30+ easy-medium problems
Days 9-10: Full mock (aptitude + technical + coding)
Days 11-12: Project prep and SQL practice
Days 13-14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock plus technical MCQ revision
Day 2 morning: 8-10 easy-medium coding problems
Day 2 afternoon: Project prep and HR rehearsal

faq.q: What is the difference between GET and JMT?
faq.a: GET is for engineering/CS graduates on the technical track; JMT is for postgraduates in any discipline, largely for PMO and business-operations roles.

faq.q: How hard is the coding round?
faq.a: Roughly LeetCode Easy-to-Medium. Solid core DSA and clean handling of test cases are enough to clear it.

faq.q: Is there negative marking?
faq.a: The aptitude test is reported to have no negative marking, so attempt all questions within the one-minute-per-question pace.

faq.q: Do backlogs matter?
faq.a: For the GET track you typically need no active backlogs and about 60% aggregate. Confirm per drive.

faq.q: Where are drives held?
faq.a: Campus drives run across cities such as Chennai, Mumbai, and Pune; off-campus roles are listed on the official careers portal.

faq.q: How many rounds are there?
faq.a: Four for GET: aptitude, technical MCQ, coding, and HR. JMT tends to weigh communication and business aptitude more.

overview: Hexaware hires engineering freshers as Graduate Engineer Trainees through a four-stage flow: an aptitude test, a technical MCQ section, a coding round, and an HR interview, with a separate JMT track for postgraduates in PMO/business-ops roles. The process is straightforward but does include a real coding round at easy-to-medium level.

comp.note: Mid-cap that pays market-competitive comp with a cloud/automation focus; entry is modest but senior and specialist bands are solid, with laterals earning premiums.

levels.note: Niche cloud/data skills lift the top
Specialist-architect or delivery-lead track reaches the peak

breakdown: Base ~85–90% of CTC; variable ~8–12%
Fresher pay: standard ₹3.5–5 LPA vs digital/cloud premium ₹6–8 LPA
Minimal fresher joining bonus; laterals negotiate joining pay
Cloud, automation, and data specialties drive the biggest raises and lateral premiums

name: Zensar
tagline: Uses a four-round funnel of online test, group discussion, technical interview, and HR, with GD sometimes skipped off-campus.
process: An online aptitude/technical test shortlists candidates for a group discussion (in some drives), followed by a technical interview and an HR round.

rounds.expect: Covers quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, verbal ability, and a coding or technical section. Serves as the first elimination filter and expects genuine coding fundamentals.
prepare: Take timed aptitude mocks
Solve easy-medium coding problems
Revise DS, OOP, and DBMS MCQs
Practice reasoning and verbal daily

rounds.expect: A GD assessing how clearly you articulate ideas, listen, and collaborate. Being able to structure your points and engage constructively matters more than dominating.
prepare: Practice speaking clearly on general topics
Learn to enter and structure a GD
Follow current affairs
Practice active listening

rounds.expect: Tests sound coding principles, data structures and algorithms, CS fundamentals, and your projects. Zensar expects a solid technical pedigree, so DSA and clean code matter.
themes: OOP and one language in depth
prepare: Practice medium DSA and clean code
Revise OOP, DBMS, and OS
Prepare project explanations
Do a mock technical interview

rounds.expect: Covers motivation, communication, relocation, and joining. Usually the final, lighter step.
prepare: Prepare a concise self-introduction
Research Zensar's business
Have consistent flexibility answers
Keep documents ready

eligibility: 60% or above in Class X, Class XII, and B.Tech, applied at each level individually (not just final aggregate). Candidates with backlogs are usually filtered at resume shortlisting before the online test. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic and DSA fundamentals
Days 4-6: Coding practice plus reasoning/verbal
Days 7-8: GD practice and current-affairs reading
Days 9-10: Full online-test-style mock
Days 11-12: DSA, DBMS, OS revision and project prep
Days 13-14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock plus 8-10 coding problems
Day 2 morning: GD practice and project prep
Day 2 afternoon: Mock technical round and HR rehearsal

faq.q: How is the 60% criterion applied?
faq.a: At each academic level individually (10th, 12th, and B.Tech), not just as a final aggregate, so a shortfall at any level can filter you out.

faq.q: Do backlogs disqualify me?
faq.a: Candidates with backlogs are usually filtered at the resume shortlisting stage, before the online test. Confirm per drive.

faq.q: Is there a group discussion?
faq.a: Yes, Zensar commonly includes a GD as a formal round, so practice structured speaking and active listening.

faq.q: How coding-heavy is Zensar?
faq.a: It expects sound coding principles and DSA, both in the online test's coding section and the technical interview.

faq.q: How many rounds are there?
faq.a: Typically four: online test, group discussion, technical interview, and HR round.

faq.q: Which DSA topics should I prioritize?
faq.a: Arrays, strings, hashing, stacks/queues, sorting/searching, recursion, and basic dynamic programming.

overview: Zensar Technologies selects freshers through an online test (aptitude plus a coding/technical section), a group discussion, a technical interview, and an HR round. It applies its 60% criterion at each academic level individually and expects sound coding fundamentals, with a GD step that makes communication a formal filter.

comp.note: Mid-tier IT services firm; pay tracks the Infosys/Wipro band but slightly below, with steep jumps only after switching or top ratings.

levels.note: Best gains come from a job switch here.
Architect track pays above PM for hot stacks.

breakdown: CTC is mostly fixed + ~10% variable; low joining/RSU component.
Fastest raises come from external offers, not internal hikes.
In-demand skills (cloud, data, SAP) command 20–40% premiums.
Onsite/client-location deputation adds allowances but not base.

name: Birlasoft
tagline: Runs a three-to-four round process: an online test with coding/technical/aptitude, then technical and HR interviews.
process: Applications are screened, then an online test covering coding, technical, and aptitude shortlists candidates for a technical interview and an HR round.

rounds.expect: Around 25 questions with multiple parts including aptitude and a flowchart section, testing numerical ability, English, and logical thinking. The flowchart component is a distinctive element testing algorithmic reasoning.
prepare: Practice flowchart-reading and logic-sequencing problems
Take timed aptitude mocks
Revise English fundamentals
Drill numerical reasoning

rounds.expect: Focuses on core languages such as C, C++, Java, and SQL, along with CS fundamentals and your projects. Be ready to explain code and write basic queries.
prepare: Revise C, C++, Java, and SQL fundamentals
Practice basic query writing
Prepare project explanations
Do a mock technical interview

rounds.expect: Covers motivation, communication, relocation, and joining. Usually the final, lighter step.
prepare: Prepare a concise self-introduction
Research Birlasoft's business
Have consistent flexibility answers
Keep documents ready

eligibility: Graduates and postgraduates who had mathematics as an academic subject; minimum 60% across academics; no backlogs; academic gap not exceeding about 1 year. Apply via the official Birlasoft careers portal. Exact criteria vary by drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: Aptitude diagnostic plus flowchart-logic practice
Days 4-5: English and numerical reasoning
Days 6-8: C/C++/Java and SQL revision
Days 9-10: Full aptitude mock including flowcharts
Days 11-12: Project prep and query practice
Days 13-14: Mock technical and HR interviews
prepC: Day 1: Aptitude mock with flowchart practice plus C/C++/Java revision
Day 2 morning: SQL practice and project prep
Day 2 afternoon: HR answer rehearsal and document check

faq.q: What is the flowchart section?
faq.a: A distinctive part of Birlasoft's aptitude test that presents flowchart-based logic to assess your algorithmic and sequencing reasoning without full coding.

faq.q: Is mathematics as a subject required?
faq.a: Many Birlasoft drives require candidates to have had mathematics as an academic subject. Confirm the specific drive's requirement.

faq.q: Which languages should I prepare?
faq.a: Core languages: C, C++, Java, and SQL, along with OOP and DBMS fundamentals.

faq.q: What are the gap and backlog norms?
faq.a: Typically no active backlogs and an academic gap not exceeding about a year. Confirm per drive.

faq.q: How many rounds are there?
faq.a: Commonly three: online aptitude test, technical interview, and HR round.

faq.q: Where should I apply?
faq.a: Use the official Birlasoft careers portal, complete your profile, and filter for fresher/entry-level roles.

overview: Birlasoft hires freshers through an online aptitude test (including a distinctive flowchart section), a technical interview on core languages, and an HR round. It commonly requires mathematics as an academic subject and enforces standard backlog and gap norms, with a compact three-round structure.

comp.note: Mid-cap IT services (CK Birla group) with strong ERP/Oracle/SAP practice; pay similar to Zensar, ERP specialists earn more.

levels.note: Enterprise ERP architects at the top.

breakdown: ERP (Oracle/SAP) functional and technical skills pay a clear premium.
Variable is modest; growth via specialization or switching.
Onsite ERP rollouts add allowances and faster promotions.
Certifications (Oracle Cloud, SAP S/4HANA) move you up a band.

name: Deloitte (India)
tagline: Runs a 4–5 stage funnel with a sectioned online assessment (including situational judgment) and multiple interviews up to partner level.
process: An online assessment covering aptitude, technical MCQs, and situational judgment leads to a technical interview, an HR/behavioral round, and often a final partner/director interview.

rounds.t: Aptitude, English, CS fundamentals and light coding under a timer
rounds.expect: A proctored MCQ-heavy test split across English/verbal, quantitative and logical reasoning, and computer fundamentals, often with 2 short coding problems for tech roles. There is typically no negative marking, so attempt everything. Sections are usually individually timed, so pace-per-section matters more than any single hard question.
themes: Data interpretation from a small table or chart
Output-prediction on a short C/Java/SQL snippet
An easy string or array manipulation coding task
prepare: Drill quant and logical reasoning free sets on IndiaBix and GeeksforGeeks aptitude pages
Solve 30-40 easy array/string problems on LeetCode or HackerRank
Revise C/Java output questions and basic SQL SELECT/JOIN syntax
Take one full timed mock to fix per-section pacing
mistakes: Spending too long on one hard quant question and starving the rest of a timed section
Skipping the coding questions because MCQs feel safer
Ignoring English/verbal, which is easy marks many candidates leave on the table
signals: Consistent accuracy across all sections, not one spiked score
Clean, compiling code on the coding tasks

rounds.t: CS fundamentals, projects, and behavioral/culture fit in one sitting
rounds.expect: A single panel blends technical questioning with HR/behavioral questions. Technical depth is fundamentals-level: OOP, DBMS, one language, and your resume projects, not competitive DSA. The same panel then probes motivation, teamwork, relocation willingness and consulting-client readiness.
themes: Walk through a project on your resume and your specific contribution
Difference between two OOP concepts with a real example
Basic SQL query and normalization reasoning
Why Deloitte and why this service line
A time you handled a deadline or team conflict
prepare: Prepare a crisp 60-second story for every resume line and project
Revise OOP, DBMS and one language's basics to explain-out-loud level
Write STAR-format answers for 4-5 common behavioral prompts
Research Deloitte's service lines and recent India focus areas
mistakes: Listing projects you cannot explain in depth
Giving vague HR answers with no concrete example
Showing no awareness of what a consulting firm actually does
signals: Clear structured explanation of your own work
Honest 'I don't know' instead of bluffing
Genuine, specific reasons for wanting Deloitte

eligibility: Typically 60% or 6.0 CGPA across 10th, 12th and graduation with no active backlogs; CSE/IT/ECE and allied branches for tech roles, broader streams for analyst roles. Confirm exact cutoffs per drive as they vary by campus and year (uncertain year-to-year).
prep2: Days 1-3: quant and logical reasoning fundamentals with daily timed sets
Days 4-6: verbal ability plus C/Java output and SQL basics
Days 7-9: 40 easy-medium array/string coding problems
Days 10-11: revise OOP and DBMS to spoken-explanation level
Days 12-13: prepare project stories and 5 STAR behavioral answers
Day 14: one full timed mock assessment plus a mock interview
prepC: Take one timed full-length aptitude mock and review every miss
Rehearse every resume project out loud plus 'Why Deloitte'
Speed-revise OOP, DBMS and SQL cheat sheets

faq.q: Is coding heavily tested at Deloitte?
faq.a: No. Expect only 1-2 easy coding problems in the online test and fundamentals-level technical questioning in the interview, not competitive DSA.

faq.q: Is there still a Group Discussion round?
faq.a: For most 2026 campus drives, no. The process now usually goes assessment straight to a combined technical-plus-HR interview, though some drives may still vary.

faq.q: Is there negative marking?
faq.a: Typically no negative marking in the online assessment, so attempt every question.

faq.q: How technical is the interview really?
faq.a: Fundamentals-focused: OOP, DBMS, SQL and your projects. It is not a LeetCode-hard round.

faq.q: How fast is the process?
faq.a: Often quick, with the interview shortly after the assessment and offers following within days to a couple of weeks.

faq.q: What matters most in the HR portion?
faq.a: Clear communication, genuine interest in Deloitte, and readiness for client-facing consulting work.

overview: Deloitte India (USI/consulting-tech) hires freshers mainly for analyst and associate-engineer tracks through a short, fast-moving funnel: an online assessment followed by a single combined technical-plus-HR interview. As of 2026 the older Group Discussion and JAM elimination rounds have largely been dropped, so the online test and one interview carry almost all the weight.

comp.note: Big-4 consulting-tech ladder; brand + structured promotion, base moderate but bonus and fast progression add up.

levels.note: Campus/lateral entry; tech consulting slightly higher.
Workstream lead; big jump from Consultant.

breakdown: Structured yearly promotions; each level is a step change, not a hike.
Variable bonus (10–25%) tied to firm and individual rating.
USI (US India) client-aligned roles can pay above domestic ones.
Top MBA/premier-college hires enter at the upper edge of each band.

name: EY (India)
tagline: Hires analysts and tech roles (including GDS) via an online assessment, an optional case/GD, technical rounds, and an HR/partner interview.
process: An online cognitive assessment leads to a group discussion or case exercise (conditional on volume), one or two technical/case interviews, and an HR or partner round on values fit.

rounds.t: Quant, verbal, logical reasoning and sometimes a technical/coding MCQ block
rounds.expect: A proctored MCQ test weighted toward data interpretation rather than raw arithmetic, with verbal and logical sections and sometimes a domain or programming MCQ block for tech roles. Typically no sectional cutoffs and no negative marking, so answer everything.
themes: Interpreting a data table to compute a ratio or growth
Basic programming or domain MCQs for the applied track
prepare: Practice data-interpretation sets daily on IndiaBix and PrepInsta free pages
Drill logical reasoning puzzles and syllogisms
Revise track-relevant fundamentals (CS basics for tech, accounting for assurance/tax)
Take one timed full mock to build speed
mistakes: Treating DI questions as pure arithmetic instead of reading the chart carefully
Leaving verbal marks on the table
Not tailoring prep to your applied service line

rounds.expect: Some drives include a group discussion or short case exercise where you analyze a business scenario in a small group. Assessors watch how you contribute, structure a point, and build on others rather than dominate. Not every drive runs this round.
themes: A business or ethics scenario to discuss as a group
Structuring an approach to a client problem
prepare: Practice speaking for 30-45 seconds with a clear point-reason-example structure
Read business and current-affairs summaries to build talking points
Practice inviting quieter members in to show collaboration
Learn a simple issue-tree framework for cases
mistakes: Dominating or interrupting to grab airtime
Making points with no structure or evidence
signals: Clear, concise contributions that move the discussion forward

rounds.t: Track domain knowledge and resume depth
rounds.expect: Content depends on your track: CS fundamentals and one language for technology roles, or finance/accounting concepts for assurance and tax. Expect resume-driven questions on your projects, internships and tools. Depth is fundamentals-solid, not competitive-DSA.
themes: Explain a project and your exact contribution
Core concept in your track (OOP/DBMS for tech, accounting standard for assurance)
A basic SQL query or a tool you listed
How you approached a problem in an internship
Trade-offs in a small design or process decision
prepare: Prepare deep, honest explanations of every resume item
Revise track fundamentals to spoken-explanation depth
For tech: OOP, DBMS, SQL and one language basics
For finance tracks: core accounting/audit concepts
mistakes: No clarity on your own project contribution

rounds.expect: A conversational round assessing why EY, career goals, willingness to relocate or work in shifts, and general communication. This is where fit for a client-service culture is judged.
themes: Why EY and why this service line
Strengths, weaknesses and a growth area
Where you see yourself in a few years
prepare: Research EY's service lines and GDS model
Prepare 4-5 STAR behavioral stories
Rehearse a genuine 'Why EY' answer
Prepare honest answers on relocation and shifts
mistakes: Generic 'big brand' reasons for wanting EY
Hesitation on relocation when the role requires it

eligibility: Typically 60% or above in 10th, 12th and graduation with no active backlogs; CSE/IT/ECE/EEE for tech tracks and commerce/finance streams for assurance and tax. EY GDS is the main fresher-hiring entity in India. Confirm exact cutoffs per drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: data interpretation and quant with timed sets
Days 4-6: verbal, logical reasoning and one full aptitude mock
Days 7-9: track fundamentals (CS or accounting) revision
Days 10-11: prepare and rehearse all resume project stories
Days 12-13: practice a group exercise and 5 STAR answers
Day 14: full mock interview covering technical plus HR
prepC: One timed aptitude mock focused on data interpretation
Rehearse project stories plus 'Why EY' out loud
Speed-revise track fundamentals cheat sheet

faq.q: What is EY GDS?
faq.a: EY Global Delivery Services is EY's captive delivery arm and the primary fresher-hiring entity in India, with major offices in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi and Kolkata.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in the aptitude test?
faq.a: Typically no negative marking and often no sectional cutoffs, so attempt every question.

faq.q: Is the group exercise always included?
faq.a: No. Some drives include a group discussion or case exercise, others skip straight to technical and HR. It varies by drive.

faq.q: How technical is the tech-track interview?
faq.a: Fundamentals-focused: OOP, DBMS, SQL, one language and your projects. It is not a competitive DSA round.

faq.q: Do non-CS branches qualify?
faq.a: Yes for many tracks; assurance and tax hire commerce/finance backgrounds, while tech tracks favor CSE/IT/ECE/EEE.

faq.q: Does EY ask about shifts and relocation?
faq.a: Yes, GDS roles can involve shifts and relocation, so be ready with honest answers.

overview: EY India hires freshers largely through EY GDS (Global Delivery Services) across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi and Kolkata for technology, assurance, tax and consulting tracks. The process is an online aptitude test followed by two to three rounds: a technical interview, an optional group exercise or case, and an HR interview.

comp.note: Big-4 consulting-tech; bands closely track Deloitte India, sometimes marginally leaner at junior levels.
breakdown: GDS (Global Delivery Services) tracks pay slightly below client-facing.
Ratings drive bonus and promotion speed; up-or-out pressure exists.
Niche skills (SAP, cyber, data/AI) get premium offers.
Lateral hires often negotiate higher than internal promotees.

name: KPMG (India)
tagline: Runs a 4–6 stage process; engineering freshers usually enter Advisory's tech/analytics practice via an aptitude test then technical and HR interviews.
process: An online aptitude assessment leads to an optional group discussion or case, then a technical interview on core CS and an HR interview on client-facing communication. Stage count varies by service line.

rounds.t: Quant, logical reasoning and verbal under time pressure
rounds.expect: An MCQ test covering quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning and often a short verbal section. The aim is speed-with-accuracy rather than trick math. Some technology drives add a short CS-fundamentals or coding block.
themes: Percentages, ratios and simple data interpretation
Short CS-fundamentals MCQs for tech roles
prepare: Practice timed quant and logical sets on IndiaBix/PrepInsta
Drill verbal ability and comprehension
For tech roles, revise OOP/DBMS MCQs
Take one full timed mock for pacing
mistakes: Losing time on one hard puzzle
Not confirming whether your drive has a coding block

rounds.expect: For tech roles the panel checks Java/OOP, DBMS theory, data-structure definitions, OS concepts and cloud basics, plus your projects. Advisory and audit tracks probe domain fundamentals. It is a fundamentals check, so clear, correct basics beat memorized edge cases.
themes: Explain OOP pillars with a real example
DBMS keys, normalization and a simple SQL query
Data structure use-cases and time complexity basics
A project walkthrough and your contribution
Basic cloud or OS concept you have listed
prepare: Revise OOP, DBMS, OS and DSA definitions to explain-out-loud level
Prepare SQL query practice
Rehearse every resume project deeply
Skim cloud fundamentals if you listed cloud skills
mistakes: Weak grasp of your own projects

rounds.expect: A conversational round assessing communication clarity, a genuine two-year plan, one real growth area, and comfort with client-facing work. Composure and professionalism matter as much as the answers.
themes: Why KPMG and why this practice
A genuine strength and a real weakness
prepare: Research KPMG's advisory and audit practices
Prepare STAR stories for teamwork and pressure
Rehearse an authentic 'Why KPMG'
Have an honest growth-area answer ready

eligibility: Typically 60% or 6.0 CGPA across 10th, 12th and graduation with no active backlogs; CSE/IT for technology roles and commerce/finance for audit and tax. Confirm exact cutoffs per drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: quant and logical reasoning timed practice
Days 4-6: verbal plus CS-fundamentals MCQs and one aptitude mock
Days 7-9: revise OOP, DBMS, SQL, OS and DSA basics
Days 10-11: rehearse all resume projects out loud
Days 12-13: 5 STAR behavioral answers plus 'Why KPMG'
Day 14: full mock covering technical plus HR
prepC: One timed aptitude mock and review misses
Speed-revise OOP/DBMS/SQL cheat sheets
Rehearse projects plus 'Why KPMG' out loud

faq.q: Is KPMG's technical round competitive DSA?
faq.a: No. It is a fundamentals check: OOP, DBMS theory, data-structure definitions, OS and cloud basics, plus your projects.

faq.q: Do technical and HR happen the same day?
faq.a: At most campuses, yes, and clearing both often leads to an offer within about a week.

faq.q: Is there always a group discussion?
faq.a: No. Some drives add a GD or short case presentation, depending on role and business unit.

faq.q: Do non-CS candidates qualify?
faq.a: Yes for audit, tax and advisory tracks; technology roles favor CSE/IT.

faq.q: What do they most want in the HR round?
faq.a: Clear communication, a genuine two-year plan, one real growth area, and comfort with client-facing work.

faq.q: Is coding in the online test?
faq.a: Some technology drives add a short CS-fundamentals or coding block, but many drives are aptitude-only. Confirm per drive.

overview: KPMG India hires freshers for advisory, technology, audit and tax roles, usually through an online aptitude test followed by a technical round and an HR round, often on the same campus day. Some drives add a group discussion or short case presentation. The technical bar is a fundamentals check, not a competitive coding marathon.

comp.note: Big-4 consulting; bands broadly match EY India, with strong risk/advisory and tech-consulting practices.
breakdown: Promotion-driven comp; annual hikes are modest between levels.
Variable pay tied to firm performance and personal rating.
Consulting/advisory tech (SAP, cyber, risk) pays a premium.
Switching among Big-4 laterally is a common way to jump a band.

name: PwC (India)
tagline: Runs a structured multi-stage graduate pipeline that can include a pre-recorded video interview and an assessment centre with group exercises.
process: After screening, an online aptitude plus technical assessment leads to interviews; some graduate programs add a pre-recorded video interview and a virtual assessment centre with group and case exercises before final interviews.

rounds.t: Numerical, verbal, inductive reasoning and situational judgement
rounds.expect: An SHL-style test with numerical reasoning (tables, charts, ratios), verbal reasoning (true/false/cannot-say from a passage), inductive/abstract reasoning, and a situational judgement section mapped to PwC's values. Some drives still use the game-based 'Career Unlocked' format.
themes: Numerical reasoning from a chart or ratio table
Situational judgement aligned to firm values
prepare: Practice SHL-style numerical and verbal tests (free samples on SHL/AssessmentDay)
Drill inductive/abstract reasoning patterns
Read PwC's values so SJT answers align
Take one timed mock to build speed
mistakes: Rushing numerical items and misreading the table
Answering SJT with what you'd really do rather than the professional ideal

rounds.expect: Where used, a set of gamified tasks measures processing speed, risk approach, memory and attention. There are no 'right' answers in the classic sense; consistency and calm focus matter.
prepare: Try free gamified cognitive assessment samples
Practice staying calm under fast timers
Sleep well and test in a quiet setting
Read up on how gamified tests score traits
mistakes: Panicking at the speed of the games

rounds.t: CS fundamentals, coding and resume depth
rounds.expect: For tech roles, expect C++/Java, OOP, DSA, DBMS/networking basics, easy-to-medium coding, occasional puzzles, and .NET or stack-specific questions depending on the role. Consulting/audit tracks probe domain fundamentals instead.
themes: Basics of a technology on your resume
prepare: Solve easy-medium coding problems on LeetCode/HackerRank
Revise OOP, DBMS and networking basics
Practice a few classic logic puzzles
Rehearse resume projects deeply
mistakes: Freezing on a puzzle instead of thinking aloud

rounds.expect: HR screens communication and confidence; a manager/AD/director may add a deeper technical or role-fit layer; and in some tracks a partner round tests poise and presence of mind. Higher rounds reward calm, structured, professional communication.
themes: Why PwC and why this line of service
Handling ambiguity or a tough client
A quick, confident answer to an unexpected prompt
prepare: Research PwC's lines of service and values
Prepare STAR stories for teamwork and pressure
Rehearse concise, confident answers
Prepare honest relocation/shift responses

eligibility: Typically 60% across 10th, 12th and graduation with no active backlogs for engineering tracks; consulting, audit and tax hire broader streams. Strong aptitude and communication matter more than prior experience for freshers. Confirm cutoffs per drive.
prep2: Days 1-3: SHL-style numerical and verbal reasoning
Days 4-5: inductive reasoning plus SJT with PwC values
Days 6-8: easy-medium coding and OOP/DBMS revision
Days 9-10: puzzles and one game-based sample
Days 11-12: rehearse projects plus 'Why PwC'
Days 13-14: mock technical plus HR/partner-style round
prepC: One SHL-style numerical/verbal timed mock
Revise OOP/DBMS and solve a few easy coding problems
Rehearse projects, 'Why PwC' and one curveball answer

faq.q: What is the game-based assessment?
faq.a: A gamified cognitive test (sometimes 'Career Unlocked') measuring traits like speed, memory and risk approach. Some drives use it, others use SHL-style tests.

faq.q: How do I handle 'cannot say' verbal questions?
faq.a: Choose 'cannot say' when the passage gives no basis to judge the statement true or false. Do not infer beyond the text.

faq.q: Is there really a partner round?

faq.a: Typically three to four: a written/online assessment, one or more technical interviews, and an HR round.

faq.q: Is the technical round competitive DSA?
faq.a: No. It is fundamentals and role-specific problem-solving, plus your projects.

faq.q: What branches qualify?
faq.a: ECE/EEE commonly for embedded and CSE/IT for software, though it varies by role and drive.

faq.q: Is coding always in the test?
faq.a: It depends on the role; some drives include a coding module and others are aptitude-plus-technical MCQ only.

faq.q: What does Cyient do?
faq.a: It is an engineering and technology services company spanning aerospace, geospatial, communications and digital, useful context for the HR round.

overview: Cyient hires freshers across IT/software and engineering/embedded roles through a written aptitude-plus-technical test, one or more technical interviews, and an HR round. comp.note: Engineering R&D / geospatial services firm; embedded/ER&D niches pay above generic IT roles.

Base-heavy CTC; domain depth matters more than tenure.
Onsite deputation (US/Europe) adds allowances and faster growth.

Practice DSA problems and SQL queries
Rehearse resume projects deeply
Prepare to reason about practical trade-offs

Prepare STAR behavioral stories

Prepare honest logistics answers

name: Nagarro
tagline: Coding-intensive hiring: a Mettl aptitude+coding test, a second pure-coding round (often graph/tree heavy), then technical and HR interviews.

Practice output-prediction questions

OOP, DBMS, and OS in depth
Debug or improve a given approach

faq.q: How hard is Nagarro's coding round?
faq.a: Genuinely demanding: about three problems spanning easy, medium, and hard. Strong LeetCode-medium practice is usually enough to clear it, with the hard problem separating top candidates.

faq.q: How many written tests are there?
faq.a: Typically two: a general aptitude plus technical ability test, and a separate coding test with three problems.

faq.q: Which DSA patterns should I prioritize?
faq.a: Sliding window, two pointers, prefix sums, hashing, recursion/backtracking, dynamic programming, and basic graphs/union-find.

faq.q: How should I allocate coding-test time?
faq.a: Secure the easy and medium problems first (roughly 20-30 min easy, 30-40 min medium) before attempting the hard one, so you do not lose guaranteed points.

faq.q: What does the technical interview test?
faq.a: Deeper DSA (often live), complexity analysis, CS fundamentals, and detailed project discussion. Explaining your approach clearly matters as much as the code.

faq.q: Do backlogs matter?
faq.a: You generally need no backlogs at the time of application. Confirm the exact rule for your drive.

overview: Nagarro runs one of the more coding-intensive fresher processes among IT firms: two written tests (general aptitude, a technical ability test, and a coding test with three problems), followed by a technical interview and an HR round. Its coding round is genuinely demanding, mixing easy, medium, and hard problems, so strong DSA is essential.

comp.note: Global digital engineering services (German-listed); pays slightly above typical Indian IT services.
breakdown: Roughly 88–92% fixed base plus annual variable pay

name: Google SWE
tagline: A first-principles coding loop that rewards clear reasoning over memorized patterns.
timeline: Recruiter → online assessment → phone screen → onsite loop → hiring committee (6–8 weeks)
process: One or two technical phone screens (medium/hard coding in a shared doc), then a virtual onsite of 4–6 rounds mixing coding, code comprehension, a Googleyness round, and (L5+) system design, ending with a central hiring committee and team match.

rounds.expect: A recruiter confirms your background, target level, timeline and location, and outlines the loop. Sometimes a soft team match is discussed. Low-stakes but sets expectations and level.

Prepare a crisp two-minute background pitch
Ask about loop format and any in-person rounds

rounds.t: DSA coding in a shared doc

Practice coding in a plain doc while narrating
Master time/space complexity analysis
Drill dry-running code by hand

rounds.expect: Two to three coding rounds on a whiteboard or shared doc covering strings, graphs, dynamic programming, sorting and shortest-path style problems. Interviewers push on optimization, complexity and correctness, and reward how you reason under hints, not just the final answer.

Optimizing a brute force to an efficient solution
prepare: Drill graphs, DP, heaps and backtracking patterns on NeetCode/LeetCode
Practice narrating trade-offs and taking hints gracefully
Time yourself at 30-35 minutes per problem
Do mock interviews (Pramp, interviewing.io free tiers)
mistakes: Freezing instead of talking through a partial idea
signals: Optimal, tested solution with complexity stated

rounds.t: Reading, debugging and optimizing code with AI assistance
rounds.expect: A newer round where you use an AI assistant (e.g. Gemini) to read, debug and optimize an existing codebase. Interviewers evaluate AI fluency: precise prompting, validating and correcting AI output, and your own debugging judgment. Availability varies by team and level (flag as evolving).
themes: Prompting the AI to locate and explain a bug
Optimizing a function with human judgment over AI output
prepare: Practice reading unfamiliar code and forming a mental model fast
Practice prompting an AI to explain/debug code, then verifying it
Build the habit of validating AI output rather than trusting it
Review debugging techniques and reading stack traces
mistakes: Blindly accepting AI output without validating
Losing your own reasoning by over-relying on the tool

rounds.expect: For L4 you may get a lighter design discussion or one embedded round; a dedicated system-design round is standard from L5 up. You scope requirements, sketch components, discuss data models, APIs, scaling, and trade-offs, driving the conversation yourself. (Weight scales with level.)
themes: Design a URL shortener or rate limiter
Design a news feed or notification system
Data model and API for a scalable service
prepare: Study the free System Design Primer on GitHub
Learn core building blocks: load balancers, caches, queues, sharding
Practice a repeatable framework: requirements, high-level, deep-dive, trade-offs
Do mock design sessions and time-box them

No discussion of trade-offs or failure modes
Letting the interviewer drive the whole session

A conflict or disagreement you resolved
Learning from a failure or mistake
Taking ownership beyond your assigned task
A time you showed curiosity or self-driven learning

Practice concise, specific, reflective delivery
Read Google's re:Work resources on collaboration
Rehearse learning-from-failure stories with real self-insight

signals: Comfort with ambiguity and bias to action

Rehearse 6 STAR Googleyness stories out loud

faq.q: Is system design tested for new grads (L3)?
faq.a: Usually not as a dedicated round. System design is standard from L5 up; L4 may see a lighter or embedded design discussion. New-grad L3 loops focus on coding plus Googleyness.

faq.q: What is the AI code-comprehension round?
faq.a: A 2026 round where you use an AI assistant like Gemini to read, debug and optimize code, evaluated on prompting, output validation and your own debugging judgment. Availability varies by team and level.

faq.q: How many coding rounds are there?
faq.a: Typically a phone screen plus two to three onsite coding rounds, all DSA-heavy.

faq.q: Can I fail on the behavioral round alone?
faq.a: Googleyness is a real signal the hiring committee weighs; strong coding with a weak behavioral read can hurt or sink a packet.

faq.q: Are interviews in India in-person now?
faq.a: As of 2026 Google often requires at least one in-person round, sometimes a split of virtual coding plus an in-person onsite. Confirm with your recruiter.

faq.q: What free resources should I use?
faq.a: NeetCode 150 and LeetCode for coding, the System Design Primer on GitHub for design, and Pramp or interviewing.io free tiers for mocks.

overview: Google's SWE loop (L3 new-grad through L4 in India) centers on strong data-structures-and-algorithms coding plus a 'Googleyness' behavioral round, with system design added from L4/L5 upward. comp.note: Top-of-market comp; heavy RSU weighting that grows sharply with level.

How you use AI tools responsibly and effectively

faq.q: Is dynamic programming tested at Meta?
faq.a: Generally no. Meta's traditional coding rounds usually exclude DP; focus on graphs, hashing, heaps, two pointers and fast implementation.

faq.q: What is the AI-enabled coding round?
faq.a: A 2026 format: a 60-minute multi-part problem (bug fix, implement, optimize) in a multi-file IDE with access to models like GPT or Claude. It tests how well you prompt, validate and correct AI output.

faq.q: Can I be rejected on behavioral alone?

faq.q: How fast is the coding pace?

faq.q: Is system design required at E5?
faq.a: Yes. Design is required from E4 up; E5 gets system design (infra) or product architecture (product roles) at senior depth.

faq.a: As of August 2026 some senior candidates skip the classic recruiter call and CodeSignal OA for an AI-native prescreener questionnaire and a 60-minute AI-native screener before the onsite. It is still evolving.

faq.q: What is the 'As Appropriate' round?
faq.a: A holistic final round run by a senior interviewer, often outside the hiring team, whose assessment carries effective veto over the decision. It blends a hard technical problem with deep behavioral evaluation.

faq.q: How important is growth mindset?
faq.a: Very. Microsoft explicitly values how you learn from mistakes and respond to hints, not just raw correctness, so stay open and coachable.

faq.q: Which DSA topics matter most?

faq.q: How should I handle interviewer hints?
faq.a: Welcome them, adjust your approach, and explain your revised reasoning. Coachability is a positive signal.

faq.q: Why does Apple feel different from Google or Meta?
faq.a: Hiring is team-owned with no central question bank, so each team writes its own questions and fit with that specific team and its domain matters heavily.

faq.q: How deep is the language questioning?
faq.a: Deep. Apple often probes core-language internals and memory behavior more than many peers, so know your primary language thoroughly.

faq.q: How important is the behavioral round?

faq.q: Is system design always included?

faq.q: How many rounds should I expect?

faq.q: How do Apple's levels work?

overview: Apple's SWE hiring is team-owned: your recruiter, screens and onsite panel all sit within the team you applied to, and each team writes its own questions with no central bank. The loop spans four to eight rounds of coding, system design (for mid-level and up) and heavily weighted behavioral, with a strong emphasis on core language depth, craftsmanship and a genuine 'Why Apple.'

name: Adobe SWE
tagline: A fundamentals-first loop with real design depth for its product suite.
timeline: Recruiter → OA → coding rounds → design → HM close (3–6 weeks)
process: An online assessment (HackerRank/CodeSignal, sometimes with CS-fundamentals MCQs) leads into 2–3 DSA coding rounds, a system design round (HLD + LLD for mid/senior), and a hiring-manager or director behavioral close; roles are titled Computer Scientist / MTS in India.

rounds.t: Baseline DSA + MCQs on CS fundamentals
rounds.expect: A timed assessment mixing 2-3 coding problems with multiple-choice questions on OS, DBMS, and networking. Passing most test cases with clean, optimized code matters more than brute force; the MCQ section is a real filter, not a formality.
themes: Array/string manipulation with an efficiency constraint
Tree or graph traversal for a hierarchy problem
MCQs on process vs thread and deadlock conditions
Networking basics: TCP handshake, HTTP semantics
prepare: Grind LeetCode easy/medium arrays, strings, trees and time yourself
Revise OS/DBMS/CN using GeeksforGeeks Gate notes (free)
Practice writing solutions that compile first-try, no library shortcuts
Do 2-3 timed HackerRank contests to build speed
mistakes: Ignoring the MCQ/fundamentals section and only prepping DSA
Submitting brute-force when an optimal solution is expected
Leaving off-by-one and null edge cases unhandled
signals: Optimal complexity reached without heavy hinting
Correct, confident answers on core CS theory
Clean variable naming and structure even under time pressure

rounds.expect: One or two live rounds with an engineer. You solve a medium problem, then handle follow-ups that push on optimality, edge cases, and sometimes a small design twist. Interviewers favor readable, optimized code over the fastest brute force.

Follow-up asking you to extend your solution to a new constraint
prepare: Practice narrating your approach before coding (NeetCode patterns, free)
Rehearse dry-running your code on examples out loud
Prepare a mental checklist for edge cases and complexity
Study one or two DS-design problems (cache, rate limiter)
mistakes: Coding before clarifying the problem constraints
Not testing your own code with a sample input
Over-optimizing prematurely instead of getting a working solution first

rounds.expect: For mid-level and above, a design round that can lean full-stack. You scope requirements, propose an architecture, and defend trade-offs. Frontend-leaning roles may go deep on component/state design; backend on data flow and scale.

API and data model for a content service
Caching and consistency for a read-heavy product
Frontend architecture for a large editor UI

mistakes: Jumping to a diagram before clarifying scope and scale
signals: Awareness of failure modes and bottlenecks

rounds.expect: A values-based conversation tied to Adobe's principles (owning outcomes, creating the future). Expect STAR-style questions about ownership, conflict, and impact, plus a deep dive into a project on your resume.

Handling disagreement with a teammate or reviewer
A failure and what you learned
Driving impact beyond your assigned scope
Why Adobe and why this team

Rehearse a 2-minute deep-dive on your strongest project

Generic 'why Adobe' with no product specificity

Genuine, researched interest in Adobe's products

topics: Arrays, strings, sliding window, two pointers

Days 9-11: System design primer + 2 mock designs

Day 14: Full mock loop; review weak areas
